# Below the match threshold, findOrCreate quietly creates a duplicate

**Claim.** A name alone never reaches the minimum match combination, so no match is attempted: the payload is stored as a brand-new person record even though the person is already in the database. There is no 'unmatched' to inspect — the no-match case is the create case.

Applies to: `~1people~1findOrCreate/post`

## Observed exchange

_The person is in the database, carrying identifiers a match could use._

```http
(setup) POST /people/create

{
  "firstName": "Harriet",
  "lastName": "Duplicata-{scope}",
  "emails": [
    {
      "email": "harriet.duplicata-{scope}@example.com"
    }
  ]
}

→ 201
  Location: https://api.securevan.com/v4/people/100000001
{
  "vanId": 100000001,
  "status": "Stored"
}
```

_findOrCreate with the name alone. Below the threshold, so: created, not found._

```http
POST /people/findOrCreate

{
  "firstName": "Harriet",
  "lastName": "Duplicata-{scope}"
}

→ 201
  Location: https://api.securevan.com/v4/people/100000002
{
  "vanId": 100000002,
  "status": "UnmatchedStored"
}
```

_Both person records now exist under the same name._
